title: Data Analytics and Integration Platform Landscape
summary: Assessment of enterprise data integration and analytics platform capabilities relevant to life sciences, covering data ontology, operational analytics, and AI/ML integration approaches.

findings.platform_architecture: Enterprise data platforms in this space use an ontology-based approach where data objects are mapped with semantic relationships. This enables cross-system queries without physical data movement, supporting regulatory traceability requirements.
findings.data_integration_model: RESTful API integration with source systems (ERP, LIMS, CTMS, CRM) using change-data-capture patterns. The integration layer maintains lineage metadata for audit purposes. Typical deployments connect 15-50 data sources in a large pharma environment.
findings.operational_analytics: Unlike traditional BI platforms focused on historical reporting, operational analytics platforms embed decision support directly into workflows — providing real-time recommendations for supply chain, clinical trial enrollment, and commercial field operations.
findings.ml_ai_integration: ML models are deployed as pipeline components rather than standalone services. This allows model outputs (predictions, classifications, anomaly scores) to flow directly into operational workflows without manual handoff.
findings.life_sciences_use_cases: Primary use cases: clinical trial site selection and enrollment prediction, drug supply chain optimization, pharmacovigilance signal detection, and commercial territory optimization. Each requires cross-domain data joining that single-purpose systems cannot provide.
findings.competitive_positioning: These platforms compete with CRM analytics by offering deeper data integration but weaker field user experience. The strategic response is platform-level data integration capabilities that match the analytical depth while maintaining the field-user-centric design.

source: Assessment of enterprise data integration and analytics platform architecture, capabilities, and life sciences use cases
